content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text bases an UNDERDETERMINED ruling on Matthew 1:16 admitting both readings, which is the single-verse/two-senses situation the rule governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings","rule_words":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open: I weighed whether this forbids marking such a verse UNDERDETERMINED, or only requires both senses to be kept, and read it as forbidding UNDERDETERMINED.","why":"The judge treats the verse's two admissible readings as a reason for UNDERDETERMINED, contrary to K-S2, which says such a verse is not open and both senses stand."}
